sentences.en: A dark chapter in a public man's history.
sentences.zh: 一位公众人物历史上黑暗的一章。

sentences.en: A pitiful story of Maria Helpin and Governor Cleveland.
sentences.zh: 关于玛丽亚·赫尔平 (Maria Helpin) 和克利夫兰州长 (Governor Cleveland) 的悲惨故事。

sentences.en: Some years ago, a beautiful, virtuous and intelligent young lady entered the employ of Flint and Kent, most excellent men and leading merchants in our city.
sentences.zh: 多年前，一位美丽、贤淑且聪慧的年轻女士进入了我们市最优秀的商人和领军人物弗林特和肯特 (Flint and Kent) 的公司工作。

sentences.en: She was put at the head of their cloak department and served them for some two or three years to perfect satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 她被任命为斗篷部门的负责人，并为他们服务了大约两三年，表现令人非常满意。

sentences.en: Mr. Grover Cleveland made her acquaintance, won her confidence, and finally seduced her.
sentences.zh: 格罗弗·克利夫兰先生 (Mr. Grover Cleveland) 与她相识，赢得了她的信任，最终诱奸了她。

sentences.en: Poor Maria Helpin, for that was her name, went away broken-hearted, disgraced and outcast,
sentences.zh: 可怜的玛丽亚·赫尔平，因为那是她的名字，心碎地离开了，蒙受耻辱，被社会抛弃，

sentences.en: while her seducer continued to revel in the realm of lust and pretend before the great American public that he is a model of virtue,
sentences.zh: 而她的诱奸者却继续沉溺于淫欲之中，并在伟大的美国公众面前伪装成道德楷模，

sentences.en: pre-eminently worthy of being honoured by their votes.
sentences.zh: 自诩极其值得选民投票支持。

sentences.en: Perhaps personal character originally ought not to be involved in political discussions, but it would be criminal to allow the virtuous to vote for so vile a man as this,
sentences.zh: 也许个人品格本不应涉及政治讨论，但如果让有道德的人去投票给这样一个卑劣的人，那将是犯罪，

sentences.en: under a false impression that he is pure and honourable.
sentences.zh: 而选民却误以为他纯洁高尚。

sentences.en: It is painful to think of his offences and shameful, infinitely shameful, to have such a man commended to the suffrages of a Christian nation.
sentences.zh: 想到他的罪行令人痛苦，而让这样一个人被推荐给一个基督教国家的选民去投票，更是可耻，无比可耻。

sentences.en: It is enough to alarm all decent people and cause even the vulgar and profane to hesitate and demand a halt.
sentences.zh: 这足以让所有正派人士感到震惊，甚至让粗俗和亵渎之徒也感到迟疑并要求停止。

sentences.en: So that, Dominic, the dramatic front page of the Buffalo Evening Telegraph on the 21st of July, 1884,
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，1884 年 7 月 21 日《布法罗晚报》(Buffalo Evening Telegraph) 那引人注目的头版，

sentences.en: breaking the news of perhaps the most lurid sex scandal in American political history.
sentences.zh: 爆出了美国政治史上或许最耸人听闻的性丑闻。

sentences.en: And that is setting the bar quite high, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这标准定得相当高，不是吗？

sentences.en: It is, because they've had some tremendous sex scandals, haven't they, in our own lifetimes, Tom?
sentences.zh: 确实，因为在我们有生之年，也发生过一些惊人的性丑闻，不是吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: There have been all kinds of goings-on in the White House.
sentences.zh: 白宫里发生过各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: I think back to the behaviour of Bill Clinton, which I think now, when you look back on it, was pretty poor.
sentences.zh: 我回想起比尔·克林顿 (Bill Clinton) 的行为，现在回过头来看，我觉得那相当糟糕。

sentences.en: I don't think there's any defending it, really.
sentences.zh: 我觉得真的没什么可辩护的。

sentences.en: And this is describing Mr. Grave Cleveland as a presidential candidate.
sentences.zh: 而这描述的是作为总统候选人的格罗弗·克利夫兰先生。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Presidential candidates being accused of sexual impropriety.
sentences.zh: 总统候选人被指控性行为不端。

sentences.en: I mean, it has been heard of, even in the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使在 21 世纪，这种事也时有所闻。

sentences.en: Even in the 21st century, there's a rich tradition of it.
sentences.zh: 即使在 21 世纪，这也有着丰富的传统。

sentences.en: But this is in a different league.
sentences.zh: 但这次的情况完全不同。

sentences.en: So on the face of it, this story is a saga of lust and lies and kidnapping and rape that is worthy of a Victorian sensational novel.
sentences.zh: 从表面上看，这个故事是一段关于欲望、谎言、绑架和强奸的传奇，足以媲美维多利亚时代的通俗小说。

sentences.en: So it often reads, for those listeners who've read The Moonstone or The Woman in White in particular by Wilkie Collins, the kind of sensation fiction of the mid-19th century,
sentences.zh: 对于那些读过威尔基·柯林斯 (Wilkie Collins) 的《月亮宝石》(The Moonstone) 或《白衣女人》(The Woman in White) 的听众来说，它读起来确实很像 19 世纪中叶的那种通俗小说，

sentences.en: there is a stolen baby.
sentences.zh: 里面有一个被偷走的孩子。

sentences.en: There is a grotesquely fat villain.
sentences.zh: 有一个极其肥胖的恶棍。

sentences.en: It's Count Fosco, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是福斯科伯爵 (Count Fosco)，对吧？

sentences.en: It's Count Fosco in The Woman in White.
sentences.zh: 是《白衣女人》里的福斯科伯爵。

sentences.en: There is a widow imprisoned in a lunatic asylum to stop her telling the truth.
sentences.zh: 还有一位被关进精神病院的寡妇，为了阻止她说出真相。

sentences.en: But also, this is a story of massive political significance because it breaks during one of the most hotly contested presidential elections in American history.
sentences.zh: 但同时，这也是一个具有重大政治意义的故事，因为它发生在美国历史上竞争最激烈的总统选举之一期间。

sentences.en: So we're in the Gilded Age, Tom, in 1884.
sentences.zh: 所以我们身处镀金时代，汤姆，1884 年。

sentences.en: And that, for people who are not massively familiar with American history, it's the era after the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 对于那些不太熟悉美国历史的人来说，那是内战后的时代。

sentences.en: It's factories, tycoons, railroads, sort of men with colossal beards, women with gigantic ball gowns.
sentences.zh: 那是工厂、大亨、铁路的时代，还有留着巨大胡须的男人们，穿着巨大舞会礼服的女人们。

sentences.en: I mean, Dominic, this is the kind of political era that Custer would have entered had he not run into the Sioux at Little Big War.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，多米尼克，如果卡斯特 (Custer) 没有在小大角战役中遇到苏族人，他本会进入的就是这种政治时代。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: So 1884 is a really, really important year because for the first time since before the Civil War,
sentences.zh: 所以 1884 年是非常非常重要的一年，因为自内战前以来，

sentences.en: the Republicans, Abraham Lincoln's party, are in real danger of losing the White House.
sentences.zh: 共和党，也就是亚伯拉罕·林肯 (Abraham Lincoln) 的党派，第一次面临失去白宫的真正危险。

sentences.en: So a generational shift politically.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一次政治上的代际更替。

sentences.en: And the man who is poised to beat them is Governor Grover Cleveland of New York.
sentences.zh: 而准备击败他们的人是纽约州州长格罗弗·克利夫兰。

sentences.en: Now, I'm guessing quite a lot of people listening to this will not really be massively familiar with his career.
sentences.zh: 现在，我猜很多听众可能不太熟悉他的职业生涯。

sentences.en: Are you familiar with his career, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你熟悉他的职业生涯吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Well, I was because he is one of those pub quiz questions that was always a banker because he was, until very recently, the only president to have served a term,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我熟悉，因为他是那种酒吧问答中总是稳拿分的题目，因为直到最近，他还是唯一一位任职一届、

sentences.en: lost an election, and then won again.
sentences.zh: 输掉选举，然后又再次当选的总统。

sentences.en: And, you know, you could go into a pub quiz knowing there was a strong likelihood that question would come up and you could bank your point.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你可以带着这种很可能会出现这个问题的预判去参加酒吧问答，然后稳拿这一分。

sentences.en: And then Donald Trump completely ruined it by doing exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 然后唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 通过做同样的事情彻底毁了这个梗。

sentences.en: Well, Donald Trump has had a pretty incredible rise to political prominence.
sentences.zh: 嗯，唐纳德·特朗普在政治上的崛起确实相当惊人。

sentences.en: But Grover Cleveland's, in some ways, is even more extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 但在某些方面，格罗弗·克利夫兰的崛起甚至更加非同寻常。

sentences.en: So at the age of 44, right, Cleveland was basically a nobody.
sentences.zh: 在 44 岁时，克利夫兰基本上是个无名小卒。

sentences.en: He was a lawyer in Buffalo, New York, quite a successful lawyer, but he'd only ever had one political job, which is the sheriff of Erie County.
sentences.zh: 他是纽约州布法罗的一名律师，相当成功，但他只做过一份政治工作，那就是伊利县 (Erie County) 的警长。

sentences.en: And he'd had that job a decade earlier and then left it and gone back to kind of his legal practice.
sentences.zh: 他在十年前做过那份工作，然后就离开了，回到了他的法律业务中。

sentences.en: And then he has this four-year period where he becomes mayor of Buffalo and then governor of New York.
sentences.zh: 然后他经历了四年的时间，成为了布法罗市长，接着是纽约州州长。

sentences.en: And then in 1884, he's nominated by the Democrats as their candidate to become the 22nd president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 然后在 1884 年，他被民主党提名为第 22 任美国总统候选人。

sentences.en: So basically, he comes from nowhere in the space of four years.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，他在四年内从无名之辈一跃而起。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a meteor, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，像流星一样，对吧？

sentences.en: And then he's president, he loses, and then he becomes president again.
sentences.zh: 然后他当上了总统，输了，然后又再次当上了总统。

sentences.en: And for about half a century after he left office, he had quite a high reputation.
sentences.zh: 在他卸任后的半个世纪里，他一直享有很高的声誉。

sentences.en: So in the 1930s, there was a very distinguished American journalist called H.L.
sentences.zh: 所以 20 世纪 30 年代，有一位非常杰出的美国记者叫 H.L.

sentences.en: Mencken who wrote, we have had more brilliant presidents than Cleveland and one or two who are considerably more profound,
sentences.zh: 门肯 (Mencken) 写道，我们有过比克利夫兰更辉煌的总统，也有过一两位更深沉的总统，

sentences.en: but we've never had one, at least since Washington, whose fundamental character was more admirable.
sentences.zh: 但至少自华盛顿以来，我们从未有过一位基本品格比他更令人钦佩的总统。

sentences.en: And I mean, that's quite a telling testimony, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这评价相当有说服力，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because Mencken was, I mean, he was a satirist as well as a journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 因为门肯，我的意思是，他既是讽刺作家也是记者。

sentences.en: He would mock what he saw as ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 他会嘲笑他认为荒谬的事情。

sentences.en: He reported on the Scopes trial, basically putting Darwinism on trial.
sentences.zh: 他报道了斯科普斯审判 (Scopes trial)，基本上是将达尔文主义送上了审判台。

sentences.en: And so the fact that he didn't see Cleveland as an immoral man or a ridiculous man, I mean, that's striking.
sentences.zh: 所以他没有把克利夫兰视为一个不道德或荒谬的人，这令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: It is very striking.
sentences.zh: 确实非常令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: But Tom, of course, if the story you opened with is true.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，当然，前提是你开头讲的故事是真的。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And then Mencken was wrong.
sentences.zh: 那么门肯就错了。

sentences.en: And if Mencken was wrong and the story is true, then Grover Cleveland was not merely a liar, a bully.
sentences.zh: 如果门肯错了，而那个故事是真的，那么格罗弗·克利夫兰不仅是个骗子、恶霸。

sentences.en: He was a sexual abuser, possibly a rapist, a man who locked his victim in a mental hospital to keep her quiet.
sentences.zh: 他还是个性虐待者，可能还是个强奸犯，一个为了让受害者闭嘴而把她关进精神病院的人。

sentences.en: So like a figure from Victorian melodrama.
sentences.zh: 就像维多利亚时代情节剧里的人物一样。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全是。

sentences.en: Now, I said, if it's true, this is the question.
sentences.zh: 现在，我说过，如果这是真的，这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: Is this story true?
sentences.zh: 这个故事是真的吗？

sentences.en: Is Grover Cleveland one of the great villains in American political history?
sentences.zh: 格罗弗·克利夫兰是美国政治史上最伟大的恶棍之一吗？

sentences.en: Or is he one of the great victims, a victim of one of its cruelest smears?
sentences.zh: 还是他是最伟大的受害者之一，是美国政治史上最残酷的抹黑手段的受害者？

sentences.en: So today's episode, it's both a brilliant window into the politics of the Gilded Age, but it's a very thrilling detective story in which you will sift the evidence.
sentences.zh: 所以今天的节目，既是一扇洞察镀金时代政治的绝佳窗口，也是一个非常惊心动魄的侦探故事，你将在其中仔细甄别证据。

sentences.en: So again, like Wilkie Collins.
sentences.zh: 所以，又像威尔基·柯林斯一样。

sentences.en: Like Wilkie Collins, exactly.
sentences.zh: 像威尔基·柯林斯，没错。

sentences.en: So maybe we should kick off with Grover Cleveland himself, because I'm guessing that a lot of listeners won't be overly familiar with the details of his career.
sentences.zh: 所以也许我们应该从格罗弗·克利夫兰本人开始，因为我猜很多听众对他的职业生涯细节不会太熟悉。

sentences.en: Grover's a great name.
sentences.zh: 格罗弗是个好名字。

sentences.en: Got to say that.
sentences.zh: 不得不说。

sentences.en: Putting that on the record.
sentences.zh: 记录在案。

sentences.en: Well, there's a muppet called Grover, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 嗯，有个布偶叫格罗弗，不是吗？

sentences.en: Who's named after Grover Cleveland, I believe.
sentences.zh: 我相信它是以格罗弗·克利夫兰的名字命名的。

sentences.en: So that's exciting.
sentences.zh: 所以这很有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is exciting.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很有趣。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So Grover Cleveland was born in New Jersey in 1837.
sentences.zh: 格罗弗·克利夫兰于 1837 年出生在新泽西州。

sentences.en: He's the fifth of nine children.
sentences.zh: 他在九个孩子中排行第五。

sentences.en: His father is a Presbyterian minister.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲是一位长老会牧师。

sentences.en: So he has a very strict Presbyterian upbringing.
sentences.zh: 所以他有着非常严格的长老会教养。

sentences.en: We're going to be sifting Grover Cleveland's kind of moral, the record of his personal morality.
sentences.zh: 我们将要仔细甄别格罗弗·克利夫兰的道德，他个人道德记录。

sentences.en: He has had a very strict Presbyterian upbringing.
sentences.zh: 他有着非常严格的长老会教养。

sentences.en: The kids in the Cleveland household weren't allowed to play on Sundays.
sentences.zh: 克利夫兰家的孩子们周日不允许玩耍。

sentences.en: They had to go to two church services, to Sunday school and to a prayer meeting on Sundays, which seems too much to me.
sentences.zh: 他们周日必须参加两次礼拜、主日学和祈祷会，这对我来说似乎太多了。

sentences.en: And all the sense that we have of him as a boy is he's actually quite dull, serious, self-disciplined.
sentences.zh: 我们对他童年的所有印象就是他其实相当沉闷、严肃、自律。

sentences.en: He's quite gruff and kind of laconic when he grows up.
sentences.zh: 他长大后相当粗鲁且言简意赅。

sentences.en: So he's not really a very flamboyant character.
sentences.zh: 所以他并不是一个非常张扬的人。

sentences.en: Could this be the mask of an unspeakable hypocrite?
sentences.zh: 这会不会是一个不可言说的伪君子的面具？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, this is the question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: So when he's 16, his father dies and a local Presbyterian deacon said to Grover, if you'd like to follow him into the church, I will pay for your education.
sentences.zh: 所以当他 16 岁时，他父亲去世了，一位当地的长老会执事对格罗弗说，如果你想追随你父亲进入教会，我会支付你的学费。

sentences.en: And Grover Cleveland said, no, it's not for me.
sentences.zh: 格罗弗·克利夫兰说，不，这不适合我。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I'm going to seek my fortune out weSt.
sentences.zh: 我要去西部寻找我的财富。

sentences.en: So off he goes.
sentences.zh: 于是他出发了。

sentences.en: And his plan, ironically, is to go to Cleveland.
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，他的计划是去克利夫兰。

sentences.en: But halfway between where he is, New Jersey or whatever, and he wants to go to Cleveland, Ohio, halfway is Buffalo, New York.
sentences.zh: 但在他所在的地方，新泽西或其他地方，和他想去的克利夫兰（俄亥俄州）之间，中间点是纽约州的布法罗。

sentences.en: And he decides to stop there because his uncle, Lewis, is there, and he's made lots of money in insurance and has set up as a farmer as well.
sentences.zh: 他决定在那里停留，因为他的叔叔刘易斯 (Lewis) 在那里，他在保险业赚了很多钱，也经营着农场。

sentences.en: Now, Buffalo is a very good place for him to be stopping.
sentences.zh: 现在，布法罗对他来说是一个很好的停留地点。

sentences.en: It is a boom town.
sentences.zh: 这是一个繁荣的城市。

sentences.en: It's a classic 19th century boom town.
sentences.zh: 这是一个典型的 19 世纪繁荣城市。

sentences.en: Buffalo is the main inland port between the Great Lakes and the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 布法罗是五大湖和大西洋之间的主要内陆港口。

sentences.en: So at this point, sort of mid-century, it's the world's largest grain port and the second largest railway hub in the whole of the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个时候，也就是世纪中叶，它是世界上最大的谷物港口，也是美国第二大铁路枢纽。

sentences.en: Is it after Chicago?
sentences.zh: 是在芝加哥之后吗？

sentences.en: I think it is after Chicago.
sentences.zh: 我想是在芝加哥之后。

sentences.en: So the west is being opened up, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以西部基本上正在被开发。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So its population has grown tenfold in 30 years, from 8 to 80,000.
sentences.zh: 所以它的人口在 30 年内增长了十倍，从 8,000 增长到 80,000。

sentences.en: It's doubling again in the next 30 years or so.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的 30 年左右，它又翻了一番。

sentences.zh: 这是一个繁荣的城市，但也是一个粗犷的城市。

sentences.en: So there's a street called Canal Street running along the Erie Canal, said to be the wickedest street in America, or people call it the infected district.
sentences.zh: 有一条沿着伊利运河的运河街 (Canal Street)，据说是美国最邪恶的街道，人们称之为感染区。

sentences.en: So maybe this is why Grover Cleveland has stopped there.
sentences.zh: 所以也许这就是格罗弗·克利夫兰在那里停留的原因。

sentences.zh: 也许吧，汤姆。

sentences.zh: 因为它两旁都是酒馆和妓院，据说比西部任何地方都危险，所以警察必须三人一组巡逻。

sentences.en: Now, if you're of Tom's more cynical disposition, you'd say, what a surprise that it's here that Grover Cleveland decides to cease his wandering.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你有汤姆那种更愤世嫉俗的性格，你会说，格罗弗·克利夫兰决定在这里停止流浪，这有什么好奇怪的。

sentences.en: Yes, escaping his mission to become a minister in the church, to settle down in a town famous for its brothels.
sentences.zh: 是的，逃避了他成为教会牧师的使命，在一个以妓院闻名的城市定居下来。

sentences.en: I think actually it's nothing to do with the brothels.
sentences.zh: 我觉得其实这和妓院没什么关系。

sentences.zh: 基本上是因为它是一个繁荣的城市，他的叔叔刘易斯说，

sentences.zh: 我会帮你找一家当地律师事务所实习。

sentences.en: And he really takes to it.
sentences.zh: 他真的很喜欢这份工作。

sentences.en: He's admitted to the New York State Bar in 1859 when he's 22.
sentences.zh: 他在 1859 年 22 岁时获得了纽约州律师资格。

sentences.en: Now, just two years later, the American Civil War is going to break out.
sentences.zh: 就在两年后，美国内战即将爆发。

sentences.en: Now, Grover is not, despite the fact that he's a Presbyterian, and Presbyterians are overrepresented in the Republican Party, he's not a Republican.
sentences.zh: 现在，格罗弗虽然是长老会教徒，而长老会教徒在共和党中比例过高，但他并不是共和党人。

sentences.en: He sees the abolitionists.
sentences.zh: 他关注到了废奴主义者。

sentences.en: He thinks they're extremists.
sentences.zh: 他认为他们是极端分子。

sentences.en: He's not a pro-slavery person, but he thinks the Democrats are more moderate.
sentences.zh: 他并非支持奴隶制，但他认为民主党人更为温和。

sentences.en: So he becomes a Democrat, and he actually campaigns for James Buchanan, one of the worst presidents in American history, in 1856.
sentences.zh: 于是他加入了民主党，甚至在1856年为詹姆斯·布坎南竞选，此人是美国历史上最糟糕的总统之一。

sentences.en: And in 1860, he doesn't vote for Abraham Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 到了1860年，他没有投票给亚伯拉罕·林肯。

sentences.en: He votes for the Democratic candidate, Stephen Douglas.
sentences.zh: 他投票给了民主党候选人斯蒂芬·道格拉斯。

sentences.en: So the war breaks out, and he doesn't fancy it.
sentences.zh: 战争爆发了，但他对此并不感兴趣。

sentences.en: Under the Conscription Act, you could pay somebody else to take your place for you if you were conscripted.
sentences.zh: 根据《征兵法》，如果你被征召入伍，可以花钱雇人代替你服役。

sentences.en: So when he is conscripted in 1863, he pays an illiterate Polish immigrant called George Biniski $150 to serve in his place.
sentences.zh: 所以当他在1863年被征召时，他花了150美元雇了一个叫乔治·比尼斯基的文盲波兰移民替他服役。

sentences.en: And later on, when this came out, because obviously it's not ideal for Cleveland's political career that he didn't serve, he is completely unrepentant.
sentences.zh: 后来这件事被曝光了，因为克利夫兰没去服役显然对他的政治生涯不利，但他对此毫无悔意。

sentences.en: He says, look, I was allowed to do it.
sentences.zh: 他说，看，我是被允许这么做的。

sentences.en: I paid this bloke.
sentences.zh: 我付钱给这家伙了。

sentences.en: I actually paid him over the odds, which is true.
sentences.zh: 我给他的钱甚至超过了市价，这是事实。

sentences.en: Cleveland paid him quite handsomely.
sentences.zh: 克利夫兰给他的报酬相当丰厚。

sentences.en: And this bloke, Biniski, later on, Republicans said, oh, this is a guy, Biniski, he served in Grave of Cleveland's place, and he went through unspeakable horrors.
sentences.zh: 后来共和党人说，比尼斯基这家伙替克利夫兰服役，经历了难以言喻的恐怖遭遇。

sentences.en: I mean, he did go through one unspeakable horror, but this was nothing really to do with the war.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他确实经历了一场难以言喻的恐怖，但这和战争没什么关系。

sentences.en: Biniski was unloading a supply wagon when, unfortunately, he suffered a testicular torsion.
sentences.zh: 比尼斯基在卸载补给车时，不幸患上了睾丸扭转。

sentences.en: What is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: It's around your testicle and sort of twists it.
sentences.zh: 就是睾丸周围的组织发生了某种扭转。

sentences.en: And unless you're operated on instantly, pretty much instantly, unless the testicle is removed, you know, you could get gangrene or you could get all sorts of horrors.
sentences.zh: 除非立即手术，几乎是必须立刻手术，否则如果不切除睾丸，你知道，可能会引发坏疽或其他各种可怕的后果。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，没错。

sentences.en: We had the guy who kills Booth cutting off his testicles.
sentences.zh: 我们之前提到过那个杀掉布斯的人切除了自己的睾丸。

sentences.en: Boston Corbett.
sentences.zh: 波士顿·科比特。

sentences.en: And now we've got another kind of Civil War period testicular theme.
sentences.zh: 现在我们又遇到了另一个南北战争时期的睾丸话题。

sentences.en: I mean, what's going on in America at this time?
sentences.zh: 我是说，那时的美国到底怎么了？

sentences.en: Yeah, something in the water, clearly.
sentences.zh: 没错，显然是水质出了问题。

sentences.en: Well, anyway, this guy had it removed, and then he was as right as rain.
sentences.zh: 总之，这家伙切除了睾丸，然后就完全康复了。

sentences.en: And Cleveland actually went and visited him in hospital, which I think reflects very well on him.
sentences.zh: 克利夫兰还去医院探望了他，我认为这对他来说评价很高。

sentences.en: Because it's not like they were great pals.
sentences.zh: 因为他们并不是什么好朋友。

sentences.en: Cleveland just paid him to take his place.
sentences.zh: 克利夫兰只是付钱让他替自己服役而已。

sentences.en: But Cleveland went to see how he was doing.
sentences.zh: 但克利夫兰还是去看了看他的情况。

sentences.en: Now, in the meantime, Cleveland's legal career is absolutely thriving.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，克利夫兰的法律事业蒸蒸日上。

sentences.en: He opens a law firm.
sentences.zh: 他开了一家律师事务所。

sentences.en: He makes loads of money.
sentences.zh: 他赚了很多钱。

sentences.en: He gets a reputation for what one of his colleagues calls his indomitable industry, his unpretentious courage, and unswerving honesty.
sentences.zh: 他以同事所称的“不屈不挠的勤奋、朴实无华的勇气和坚定不移的诚实”而闻名。

sentences.en: Dominic, could I read you something from the Bodleian?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我可以给你读一段博德利图书馆的资料吗？

sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Wikipedia features.
sentences.zh: 维基百科特辑。

sentences.zh: 我们好久没在历史节目里用维基百科了。

sentences.en: So this is what it says in the Bodleian.
sentences.zh: 这是博德利图书馆里的记载。

sentences.en: Yeah, go for it.
sentences.zh: 好，读吧。

sentences.en: Cleveland assumed a lifestyle of simplicity, taking residence in a plain boarding house.
sentences.zh: 克利夫兰过着简朴的生活，住在一间普通的寄宿公寓里。

sentences.en: He devoted his growing income to the support of his mother and younger sisters.
sentences.zh: 他将日益增长的收入用于供养母亲和年幼的妹妹们。

sentences.en: But again, what if it's all a front?
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，如果这一切只是伪装呢？

sentences.en: Well, but this all makes him sound incredibly dreary.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但这让他听起来极其乏味。

sentences.en: It does, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 确实是这样，不是吗？

sentences.en: But he's not, actually.
sentences.zh: 但实际上他并非如此。

sentences.en: He's a great laugh.
sentences.zh: 他是个很有趣的人。

sentences.en: So places like Buffalo Boomtowns are full of bachelors of this, of sort of in their 20s and 30s, because men greatly outnumber women.
sentences.zh: 像布法罗这样的繁荣城镇里到处都是二三十岁的单身汉，因为男性人数远多于女性。

sentences.en: And Cleveland is a proper man's man.
sentences.zh: 而克利夫兰是个地地道道的“男人中的男人”。

sentences.en: So he will spend his evenings.
sentences.zh: 所以他会花时间在晚上。

sentences.en: When he's not working, he goes to a saloon or a beer hall.
sentences.zh: 不工作的时候，他会去酒馆或啤酒屋。

sentences.en: He smokes cigars.
sentences.zh: 他抽雪茄。

sentences.en: He plays poker with the lads.
sentences.zh: 他和伙计们玩扑克。

sentences.en: He just has a brilliant time.
sentences.zh: 他过得非常精彩。

sentences.en: He's barely straining against the buttons of his florid waistcoat.
sentences.zh: 他那华丽的背心扣子都快被撑开了。

sentences.en: He looks exactly as he should.
sentences.zh: 他看起来完全就是那副样子。

sentences.en: So he's an enormous man, six feet tall.
sentences.zh: 他是个大块头，身高六英尺。

sentences.en: He's got a gigantic walrus moustache.
sentences.zh: 留着巨大的海象胡子。

sentences.zh: 当时布法罗成了德国移民的热门聚集地。

sentences.en: So there are loads of German beer halls and places serving sausages.
sentences.zh: 所以那里有很多德国啤酒屋和供应香肠的地方。

sentences.en: And this is basically Cleveland's diet.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是克利夫兰的饮食。

sentences.en: So Cleveland starts to become incredibly fat.
sentences.zh: 所以克利夫兰开始变得非常肥胖。

sentences.en: His friends call him either Big Steve or Uncle Jumbo.
sentences.zh: 他的朋友们叫他“大史蒂夫”或“珍宝叔叔”。

sentences.en: So here he is, Uncle Jumbo or Big Steve.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他，珍宝叔叔或大史蒂夫。

sentences.en: And everybody thinks he's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 大家都觉得他很棒。

sentences.en: He's a great fan.
sentences.zh: 他是个大粉丝。

sentences.en: He loves a sort of a tall tale, a massive cigar, all of this.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢吹牛、抽粗雪茄，诸如此类。

sentences.en: The only thing that diminishes his sense of genial swagger, Tom, he's basically got, I hate to say this, he's got your voice.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，唯一削弱他那种亲切狂妄感的是，我不想这么说，但他有你的那种嗓音。

sentences.en: Oh, manly.
sentences.zh: 哦，很有男子气概。

sentences.en: People say he's got a voice that's perhaps slightly more sensitive than you would expect from such a big man.
sentences.zh: 人们说他的声音比你预想中那种大块头应该有的声音要稍微敏感一点。

sentences.en: Does that seem fair to you?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这公平吗？

sentences.en: There's nothing wrong with that.
sentences.zh: 那没什么不好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So on the one hand, he's very boring and lives a life of simplicity.
sentences.zh: 所以一方面，他非常无聊，过着简朴的生活。

sentences.zh: 另一方面，他又出去大口吃香肠，和伙计们混在一起。

sentences.en: They seem hard to integrate.

sentences.en: So he's living his life of austerity.
sentences.zh: 所以他过着苦行僧般的生活。

sentences.en: And then he's going out on the town.

sentences.en: I think he works hard and blaze hard.

sentences.en: That's what he does.

sentences.zh: 奥斯卡·福尔瑟姆比克利夫兰更像个浪子。

sentences.zh: 他喜欢打猎和赌博。

sentences.en: Oh, like Prince Philip.
sentences.zh: 哦，就像菲利普亲王那样。

sentences.en: So meanwhile, Grover's had this little dabble in politics.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，格罗弗在政界小试牛刀。

sentences.zh: 布法罗民主党发展得很好，因为它特别吸引移民，比如爱尔兰移民、德国移民等等。

sentences.en: The Republican Party had always had a nativist element to it, so immigrants tend to be drawn to the Democrats.

sentences.zh: 他在所有好友的簇拥下宣誓就职。

sentences.zh: 你会绞死他们吗？

sentences.en: What do you do?
sentences.zh: 你会怎么做？

sentences.zh: 他为此挣扎过。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's not a murderer.

sentences.zh: 好吧，我还在想这是否反映出他有一种以

sentences.en: Okay, I'm just, you know, groping my way to try and get a handle on his character.
